en: Udāna 2.1 Mucalinda Sutta Thus have I heard—
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Uruvelā on the bank of the river Nerañjarā at the foot of the Mucalinda tree, having just attained full enlightenment.
Now at that time, the Blessed One remained seated cross-legged for seven days, experiencing the bliss of liberation.
At that very time, a great unseasonable storm arose, a seven-day downpour with cold winds and overcast skies.
Then the Naga king Mucalinda, having emerged from his own abode, coiled his coils seven times around the Blessed One’s body and stood with his great hood spread over the Blessed One’s head, thinking:
"May there be no cold for the Blessed One; may there be no heat for the Blessed One; may there be no contact with gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, sun, or creeping creatures for the Blessed One.
Then, at the end of those seven days, the Blessed One arose from that meditative concentration.
Then the Naga king Mucalinda, perceiving that the sky was clear and free of clouds,
uncoiled his coils from the Blessed One’s body, withdrew his own natural form, manifested the form of a young brahmin,
and stood before the Blessed One with palms joined in reverence, paying homage to him.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“Seclusion is bliss for one who is contented,
who has heard the Dhamma, and who sees.”
Harmlessness is happiness in the world,
restraint toward living beings;
dispassion toward the world is happiness.
The transcending of sensual desires,
and the subduing of the conceit "I am"—
this indeed is the supreme happiness.
The first.
